title: Quality and speech analytics
summary: Evaluation forms, AI scoring, topics and programs, and the limits on the speech-analytics articles.

lessons.title: Quality evaluates the interaction. Speech analytics reads it
lessons.summary: The quality article says speech and text analytics runs on 100 percent of interactions. That is a claim to re-open, not a sample size you invent.
paras: The about-quality-management article says quality management lets managers record and evaluate agents and interactions, and coach them. Its administration list includes evaluation forms, weights, policies, and exporting recordings to AWS. Its evaluation list includes a dashboard, scoring, calibration, monitoring in-progress interactions, annotations, assignees, and disputes. Coaching appointments are a separate section on that page.

The same article says speech and text analytics provides automated analytics on 100 percent of interactions. This chapter uses that sentence as the article’s scope, not as a guarantee this lab measured. The quality track in the lab already walks forms, policies, and coaching at a high level. This chapter goes into the automation options, the topic dictionary, and the program limits.

lessons.title: A question is human, AI scored, or assisted by topics
lessons.summary: The form article names three automation choices. Evaluation focus is Full Interaction or Evaluated Agent.
paras: The create-and-publish article, as the automated-scoring article points at it, gives each question one of three choices: No Automation, AI Scoring, or Evaluation Assistance. No Automation is a person. AI Scoring is a model. Evaluation Assistance uses speech and text analytics topics to select the answer. Both AI Scoring and Evaluation Assistance support voice and digital interactions, on the automated-scoring article.

When you add the question, that article also asks for an Evaluation Focus: Full Interaction or Evaluated Agent. Publishing is still required for the form to be used. The quality article’s list includes weights, copying a form, and assigning an evaluation. This lesson does not invent point values. If a weight is not on the page you have open, leave it off the design.

lessons.title: AI scoring waits for history, and a low week hides the answer
lessons.summary: A rolling window of 25 submissions. Below 75 percent, the answer is hidden. The transcript needs 300 characters.
paras: The automated-scoring article says AI scoring runs only when the conversation meets at least one of its criteria, and the criterion written in the notes this lab could read is a transcript of at least 300 characters. If the criteria are not met, it does not evaluate. Questions and each answer are limited to 500 characters. Help text is limited to 6,000. You can save at most five answer options. The model’s text must match an answer exactly, including accents.

Accuracy is how often people change the AI answer. The window is the 25 most recent submissions for that question. At 75 percent or above, the answer is shown. Below 75 percent, the question is flagged low-confidence and the answer is hidden, while Genesys Cloud keeps storing the model’s response. The flag clears when the same window rises above 75 percent again. Republishing the form resets that history. History for a quiet question is deleted after 30 days without activity. The prerequisites named on the page are CX 1 WEM Add-on II, CX 2 WEM Add-on I, CX 2, CX 3, or CX 4, the evaluation-form permissions it lists, and AI Experience Tokens.

lessons.title: Phrases make a topic. Topics make a program
lessons.summary: A program is mapped to queues or flows, and it can turn sentiment and empathy on or off.
paras: The programs, topics, and phrases article defines the dictionary. A phrase is a string of words for one way to say something, typed one by one or uploaded, and words outside the standard dictionary are added to the language model. A topic is a collection of phrases for a business intent, such as cancellation. A program is a package of topics mapped to queues or flows, and it may contain more than one language or dialect. The program can enable or disable customer sentiment analysis and agent empathy analysis for its own interactions.

Evaluation Assistance uses those topics as conditions. The automated-scoring article says a topic cannot appear in more than one condition, and only one answer on a question can have assistance conditions. If several topics sit in one Includes condition, one match makes the condition true. If several sit in one Excludes condition, the condition is true only when all of them are absent. When a question has several conditions, every condition must be true before the answer is filled in.

lessons.title: Programs have counts, and the organization switch wins
lessons.summary: One hundred programs. Five hundred topics per dialect. Twenty scoring rules. Sentiment off at the org turns it off everywhere.
paras: The work-with-a-program article’s create section states these limits: 100 programs in the organization, 20 tags on a program and on a topic, 500 queues and 500 flows on one program, and 20,000 queues and flows for the whole system. The program name is case sensitive and limited to 100 characters. The description is limited to 10,240 characters. A tag name is case sensitive and limited to 100 characters. Topic limits on the same article: 500 topics per dialect, 15 dialects in the editor, and you cannot publish a program that contains more than 500 unpublished topics. A program can include up to 20 enabled agent-scoring rules.

You save a draft, then publish. The program uses the topic version that was current at publish time. A default program with predefined topics is included. Quality administrators can manage queues, flows, and scoring, and cannot change speech and text analytics settings. In Genesys Cloud EX, programs map to queues only; picking a flow has no effect. Customer sentiment and agent empathy are on by default. If either is disabled for the organization, the program control is unavailable and the analysis does not run, while the program’s own saved choice is kept for later.

lessons.title: Agent scoring picks which agent receives the evaluation
lessons.summary: Each, first, or last matched agent. The article also says the last participant is the evaluated agent.
paras: The program article’s agent-scoring section lists three generation choices: Each Matched Agent creates an evaluation for every matched agent, First Matched Agent only the first, and Last Matched Agent only the last. A later sentence on the same page says the last agent to participate is assigned as the evaluated agent. Read both sentences against the control you are about to set, because this lab will not collapse them into one rule.

Automated scoring there uses a published agent auto-evaluation form. For digital interactions, the article says evaluations are regenerated when a new response is added to the thread. Calibration, disputes, and coaching remain the quality article’s process names. This lesson does not invent a calibration agenda. The quality track is where the coaching loop is practiced.
